notes:
Summary: Mid-market product company building a guided-help/support assistant + internal search/reranking across product docs. Currently on another LLM API provider (OpenAI-style). Exploring Redwood Hosted first (fast onboarding) then Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.

Key quotes / takeaways: 
- "We need prompt parity — answers must match current tone and extraction behavior" (Head of ML).
- "If we can get 30-40% cost savings at scale and p95 latency <150ms we're in" (VP Product).

Technical constraints / asks:
- Wants an OpenAI-compatible compat layer to minimize client-side changes (existing SDKs, prompt templates).
- Prompt templates + few-shot examples used heavily; worried about subtle regressions after model swap. Require regression testing harness.
- Throughput target: 200 qps for chat/assist; batch embeddings job nightly for 1.2M documents.
- Latency target: chat p95 < 150ms on Dedicated profile, p50 < 70ms.
- Need per-route cost breakdown and token-level tracing during POC.
- Data controls: SSO, audit logs, KMS integration. Prefer VPC peering for Dedicated.

Commercial / process notes:
- POC agreed: 4-week Hosted POC focusing on parity + perf. Team will run eval prompts and synthetic load.
- If Hosted POC acceptable, move to Dedicated pricing proposal (committed capacity).
- Procurement timeline compressed: aiming for Q2 deployment.

Risks/Concerns captured in calls:
- Regression risk during model parity -> smallest diffs lead to UX friction. Need canary and A/B test paths.
- Compatibility mapping work could add 2-3 weeks to engineering integration (mapping functions + errors).

References: Gmail threads and Drive deck contain current prompt templates and evaluation harness (see Drive). Fireflies call ff_20260218_5691 contains demo notes where we saw initial hallucination cases on one system prompt.
